data: Great story, great gameplay, perfect soundtrack
Beautiful, amazing, so fun, so well balanced, expert mode felt so GOOD to play with
Incredible Music: The soundtrack is phenomenal
Loving the game so far and I really hope they add more content to it
That didn’t help much because the writing is boring and repetitive too
That didn’t help much because the writing is boring and repetitive too
Great game. Great music. Great gameplay. Great characters. Above average story. Definitely recommend for any jRPG or Final Fantasy enjoyer.

I'm so glad Asians are in charge of making AAA games again. Pearl Abyss giving us Crimson Desert, and now, Square Enix LANCARSE giving us this FF game. My God we are eating good!!!! FF Resonance is a masterpiece of a game.

YES, it feels like an old comfort Final Fantasy with a bit of modern mechanics and QoL.
Will update later.

Bit of a Neutral response. I was playing the game on PS5 with no issues, but wanted to play on the Steam Deck so grabbed the Steam version. All in all it plays fine, but it will lock when skipping cutscenes, particularly the cutscenes that precede the QUEST ACCEPTED text for sidequests. Pretty annoying, and so far subpar to the PS5 version.

Game is a masterpiece and well worth it. The HD-2D caught me by surprise with how beautiful they can make the game look while still keeping that retro feel and being turn based only adds to that retro feel. Has a great cast of characters with a beautifully written story. Would also like to include that it has many great voice actors. With a couple of them being personal favorites like Clifford Chapin, Jonah Scott, and Ian Sinclair. Overall one of my favorite FF titles in a while.

This game is nostalgia bait done right. Classic turn based battles that are fun and challenging and a full party of eventually 8 separate characters, a story that doesn't break new ground but is solid everywhere nonetheless given its a retelling of an already established defunct mobile game, memorable characters and emotional storytelling that is well written and pulls at your heartstrings as well as hype moments that just slap (the OST in this game rocks), a great twist on the job system with the addition of Visions, and a genuinely awesome world with lots to find and explore (the airship flying takes me back to the simpler times of classic FF) truly I have enjoyed this game immensely and I hope Square Enix decides to go back to its roots with FF after the success of Resonance. 10/10.

(Re-edit after getting the platinum trophy) Yeah this game was a blast man, truly I hope it gets nominated for JRPG of the year.

This game is amazing! It blends 2d and 3d much better than other similar games I’ve played in the past. I normally enjoy jrpgs, but tend to frequently bounce off of them. This one on the other hand has kept me hooked.

9/10

This has been my favorite Final Fantasy game since X. This was a true callback to the OG type of FF that I missed and loved.

This game was a true cherry on top for fans that wanted classic turn based. I wish they would have made it and brought back how X had it's combat system. You can switch party members in and out of combat at will and see the turn base order. They had the turn base order, but imagine all the possibilities and fights if you could swap your party members depending on the battle.

The vision system was an excellent choice, but I feel like they needed more white mage types and they added a lot of commando's that had near the same kit. Felt a bit repeatitive for some of them. If they do any sequels or continue off the success of this game, I would not mind more antagonists such as Kefka or side party members like Ashe from XII, Red from VII making an appearance as a vision in a future game.

Overall, very enjoyable story and gameplay. Will gladly buy another should it come out in the future.

A very solid classic final fantasy experience in a more modern style, this game will be great for challenge runs and has so much replay-ability. For a remake of a gatcha phone game this is amazing but it's origin comes with some shortcomings via story. highly recommend for those who know ff very well, a bad start for new ff players

I haven't played FFBE but I have always wanted to experience its story. This is the perfect game for that with the classic FF formula.

Not everything is voiced but I really don't mind the reading (if anything it feels really like playing the old FFs on PS1 before voiced dialogue existed). The story is very intriguing and I am very glad SE adapted the mobile game into a proper game.

While I don't mind the more ARPG direction of the recent mainline titles, it really does scratch that itch when SE also make a standard turn-based RPG FF with its classic elements. Familiar battle systems their unique spin (visions), unique party members and the top notch music just make this a very enjoable game.

I really hope they don't just stop there and green lit a second game revolving around the second season of FFBE.

Honestly a great game. I definitely prefer final fantasy games as turned based adventures. The gameplay is the job system of bravely default (visions) combined with the stagger system from ff13. It feels good to make builds and level up visions to access more abilities. The story is fine, its nothing revolutionary compared to other FF titles but it also doesnt drag and carries you through the game at a good pace. If you like final fantasy and want the feel of a square turned based RPG I highly recommend this game.

Came in expecting a lazy asset flip, but pleasantly surprised; This is instead a well-designed, lovingly-crafted, wholly transformative asset flip.

Brilliant, fun, whimsical, not overly complex, still occasionally challenging, and just the right amount of charm.

+++ Buildcrafting is great.
++ OST is awesome.
+ Doesn't take itself overly seriously.
-- English VA is a mixed bag with some standouts and some dogshit. JP recommended as is the sane thing to do as with anything where it's an option vs American VO.
- Early exploration is railroaded.
- Not the most balanced. You can optimize the fun encounter design away if you use broken builds.

The game has changed its general mechanics from the mobile version, but it kept alive the customization aspects for your team. Turn based combat was altered slightly. I am glad to have the voice acting for the main story as well.

When Brave Exvious came out on mobile, I remember thinking that they should make this into a stand alone because it doesn't deserve to be just a mobile game. Man, this is everything I wanted. This is a love letter to all of the old games. If you an old school ff fan, this game is a must play!

It feels like a loveletter from a final fantasy fan in square enix. Who had the thought of a Game wich goes back to the basics but not to simplify it. Mixed it with nostalgie, a banger soundtrack and a class system that i would love to see in future games from the ff franchise.
Feels mostly like the final fantasy i grew up with so much fun! such a good game. a little story lite but since it was converted from a gotcha game not bad a t all!

I'll leave this as positive but will change if my opinion changes.

Graphically the game does 2.5D really well, the 3D animations for the cameos in battle I think look a bit uncanny but that's fine, you can skip them. Combat is decent, not overly complex but not braindead simple either. Story has been alright so far, nothing to write home about and I think pretty run of the mill for a Final Fantasy game. Character's are fine, nothing special much like the story.

Game has been enjoyable though, there's reasons to go explore every point of interest and the progression mechanics keep you engaged. The class system is a bit different and being able to pick and choose abilities passives from multiple visions lets you build your characters however you want which is nice.

Only main gripe I have is how much this game babies you, everything is spoon fed to you like crazy, there is 0 chance you'd miss anything in this game or get stuck. It's also been extremely easy so far, but nonetheless the game is good.

Final Fantasy Resonance was a great time overall. The combat feels fantastic — fast, flashy, and satisfying — and the graphics are genuinely stunning, easily some of the best in the series. The cinematic cutscenes are a real highlight.

The story is where the game stumbles a bit. It's serviceable and keeps things moving, but it plays things pretty safe — not many surprises or big twists along the way.

That said, the overall package absolutely won me over. If you're here for gorgeous visuals, great combat, and a fun ride, you won't be disappointed. 

A No-Brainer for any Final Fantasy VI fan.
Its just nostalgia bait with an okay story, but its a good time all the same. Headsup if you don't want spoilers for every mainline FF game ever made, the game basically spoils the lot.

The game really captures the old RPG feel, turn based battles, exploring the overworld, leveling characters and visions, finding items in hidden pathways. Character voice acting and animations done very well, boss fights are fun and exciting, the story while simple is satisfying enough to keep interest. Definitely a recommended title if you looking an older style RPG.

This is the Final Fantasy we’ve been waiting for! The classic gameplay, the adventure, and that good old JRPG feeling are finally back. This is what Final Fantasy should feel like! It feels like coming home to the series we fell in love with. The real Final Fantasy is back!

10/10. hope for more like this in the future!

10/10 Final Fantasy Game! I really wish they would remake the older games in the same style as this. The combat feels so oldschool Final Fantasy, I had the feeling I was playing FF 6. Story is just a typical Final Fantasy as well and oh my the Graphics. I love the 2DHD style. PLEASE give us FF 1 - 6 in this style.
It was such a great game. Since FFBE have several seasons, I really hope we get a sequel someday.
If you love Final Fantasy, this is a game you absolutely must play. Do yourself a favor and buy this game. You're welcome, no thanks necessary.

I am not really a Final Fantasy fan. but I am started to become one. Especially while playing this game.
It's clearly a love letter to the past games. It looks great and plays great as well.
The story so far is interesting and the characters are likeable. Voice acting is as always perfect and the music is great as always as well.

This is one of those games you start playing and can't put down. Would highly recommend for both fans and non fans of Final Fantasy games. It's that good!

This is a very good game. It's visually stunning, the music is fantastic, and it's a fun and interesting journey from start to finish.

My only real critique is that it relies too much on nostalgia and doesn't really establish its own identity or leave you with anything new. It's main themes become very confused and get lost in their own sauce. It wants to simultaneously have the story of every other Final Fantasy game, while never really committing to having its own, so by the end it winds up feeling as if it were about like 15 different stories all at once. 

It kinda works, but it's also very fatiguing, confusing, and cliche. I didn't dislike it as a whole and would definitely recommend it to any Final Fantasy enjoyer, but I'm not sure if I would recommend it if you don't already enjoy other games in the series. Go play those instead, they have a lot more to offer.

This game is a love-letter to the NES/SNES era of Final Fantasy. The HD-2D presentation is amazing, the soundtrack is legendary, and the battle system and gameplay at Expert difficulty is awesome. A game for the fans - it has soul.

If you have any love for old school Final Fantasy, this is a must play.

Demo progression carries over to the full game, so go try the demo! It's about 4 to 5 hours long!

The voice acting is fantastic. They really poured out their hearts to the characters. Combat is so good, I didn't mind running in circles to grind for more XP and ability unlocks.
Story is quite simple, yet good and it has glorious hype moments, where one would ascend.

This is not only nostalgia, it's a perfect RPG game itself. One fit for the classic Final Fantasy-Fans as well. Please add the rest of the story and you will have more of my money!

Boots on the ground for the fans!

I don't think FF Resonance is a bad game. Far from it. It's visually stunning, with some of the best pixel art I've seen in a game. I even enjoy its nostalgia-driven Vision system, and exploring its world is genuinely fun. Yet, for all its charm, it's an incredibly unremarkable experience.

The story is clichéd and uninspired, even by the standards of the classic Final Fantasy titles it so desperately tries to emulate. Its characters are one-dimensional, serving little purpose beyond moving the plot forward. The game seems so preoccupied with recreating the appeal of its predecessors that it forgets to establish an identity of its own. It plays everything safe, offering little that hasn't already been done, often better, decades ago.

Perhaps I would have given it a thumbs up if it didn't carry the Final Fantasy name. But then again, without that name, I probably wouldn't have bothered playing it in the first place, much like the countless other mediocre Square Enix games that have come and gone.
So far I am loving it, feels like a classic with a modern twist, reminds me of gaming when I was young.

Story is pure JRPG cheese, but the nostalgia-laced Visions are cool. Classic turnbased combat goodness. Great HD2D visuals. Excellent FF vibes.

At the end of the day, there's a demo. Play it. If you like it, buy the game and progress transfers.

The game was good, the mid-game story was interesting, and the progression was enjoyable, but the ending is an absolute disaster.

the story and dialogues are ridiculously cheesy, slow, and drawn-out. And when I say long, I mean LOOOOOOONG!

Even when I was already losing my mind, I was still only 30% of the way through!

It completely ruined the experience for me.

The magic just wasn't there. We're nowhere near the masterpieces that were Final Fantasy VII, VIII, IX, and X.

Square Enix has NAILED this one. Great, self-contained smaller adventure with characters that don't feel one-note. The "visions" system almost functioning as a pseudo jobs system adds to the variety of the older turn-based style. The pixel art and soundtrack are both top level. For people who enjoy the classics, this is something worth experiencing.

I just love this game even though I just reached Act 3, this might become one of my favourite games of all time. Lovely music and art. The mix of Pixel 2D Sprites and a gorgeous 3D world fits so well.
Love the gimmick of bringing back charachters from past Final Fantasy games as 'stands'. My only complain is when introducing these characters you might get minor spoilers for those games, but well some of them are decades old, we've had enough time to play them.

DAYUM...

It's been a while since I played a Final Fantasy this good. SERIOUSLY!

The game just... Works.

If you are a fan of the series, I recommend it.
Wow It reminds me so much of my childhood. The graphics are superb. The turn based combat is so in dept and should of been in the seven remake. If you are a fan off the old school ff games buy it.

Grew up in the 90s playing and replaying SNES JRPGs. Final Fantasy VI is one of my favorite games of all time.

I'm seeing a lot of hate on Resonance for it's mobile gaming roots, which made me skeptical as well. However, I gave it a chance on Jason Schreier's glowing recommendation, and I agree with him: they should have called it Final Fantasy 17.

It's a modern SNES Final Fantasy. It was rebuilt from the ground up and in no way resembles a cheap mobile game.

I was never a fan of JRPGs but was always intrigued by the art of final fantasy so i decided to give this game a go and now i just can't stop playing this game. Everything about this game is great: the music, combat, stories, characters, pacing, side quests stories, worldbuilding, visuals... literally everything is a masterpiece and it is also a very good introductory game to learn more about the world of final fantasy. In fact, this game has piqued my interest towards the other FF games and I am a happier man after experiencing this masterpiece. Thank you to everyone who worked on and created this game.

100/10 Highly recommend!

People who claim it's just the cell phone gatcha rereleased have no idea what they are talking about. It has been rebuilt from ground up to be a very enjoyable experience. If you like turn based games I highly recommend you play this one.

This game is what Final Fantasy Brave Exvius could have been and SHOULD HAVE BEEN. 
The story at its core was always rich enough, to carry itself without the need for PREDATORY MICROTRANSACTIONS and PAY-TO-WIN MECHANICS, that absolutely ruined the game when it was on mobile primarily. 
Kudos to whomever at SquareEnix made the decision, to remake FFBE and make it playable on PC. 
If I could give this game 11 out of 10 stars, I would.

As a long-time FFBE player, experiencing this game was a nostalgic journey. The original mobile title was my gateway into the classic Final Fantasy universe. Seeing it transformed into a wonderfully polished, standalone experience is exactly what the game deserved.

A good, but not great game for anyone whose been looking to scratch a JRPG itch. It's paced quite well, which I find to be a major problem with Square games since the PS2 era. The story is decent once it gets going, but I find the characters to be overly reliant on anime tropes. The relationship between the two main male characters was particularly bad.

The closest game I can compare this to is simpler and shorter version of Tri-Ace's Star Ocean 2 for what it's worth.

It feels like I am playing Final Fantasy V and VI for the first time, and it is truly amazing to have that feeling again. Everything about the game (including the writing) feels like it came from a classic Super Nintendo Final Fantasy with updated modern controls and visuals. For better or worse the game plays like a traditional Final Fantasy game that I grew up with, and I couldn't be happier.
Thank you Square for going back to your roots. Lots of good things in this game and hoping they will pass the torch to the main series.

Wow, i can't describe anything cause i beat the game and it's spoiler heavy for anything that isn't what you'll see in the trailer, but even for the people that avoid trailers i see you.

It's WORTH the price, get it, love it, you'll have no regrets. 10/10

Always liked FF games, the remake of FF7 is amazing but a clusterfuck of minigames.. it is a slog, this one is just old school with references to all other FF games, its 10/10 in everyway. No billion side quests, no hack and slash.. just old school rpg. <3

Thank you square. Please look to this game and realize that truly turn based ff isn't unwanted or dead and I don't need every game to be turn based but once in awhile it would be nice. Truly a beautiful ending.

Scratching that old-school FF itch... but damn! Let us disable the pop-ups and speed up the after fight screen! I don't see why the different totals and exp bars can't be just done on 1 screen which you can end with 1 or 2 clicks? Just too much clutter in that and menus. Those complaints aside, fantastic game so far and runs great on the Steam Deck. I'm gonna go play now. OK bye now.

FINAL FANTASY BRAVE EXVIUS Minus GACHA 

As a FFBE Veteran, this game has everything and more of classic Final Fantasy of the past with 2D HD Aesthetics. 

I highly recommend play the Free Demo before purchasing the full game. Demo Datais transferable to the Full game.

You wont be disappointed...except wishing this should be called FF17
